coordinates.note: The coordinate is the OpenStreetMap/Nominatim polygon centroid of the whole Fermilab campus (about 27 km2), not a surveyed position of any detector hall, so it is recorded as a campus point and shown as approximate. The site is the placement of several Fermilab short- and long-baseline detectors (DUNE near detector, ICARUS, SBND, MicroBooNE, MiniBooNE, MINOS near detector, NOvA near detector, MINERvA). LBNF/DUNE's 'excavations and structures' page, its FAQ and the Fermilab design reports (checked 2026-09-17) give no latitude and longitude for the near-detector hall, only that it is near Kirk Road and Giese Road, 60 m underground; fnal.gov refuses automated requests. Treat every placement here as campus-precision.

name: Fermilab main campus, Batavia, Illinois
notes: Coordinates are shown at campus precision; see the coordinate note. The marker is not a claim of survey-grade precision for any one hall.

summary.plain: The 27-square-kilometre laboratory site west of Chicago where Fermilab accelerators, the neutrino beamlines and the DUNE near detector are located.
summary.technical: Surface campus in Batavia, Illinois hosting the Fermilab accelerator complex (linac, Booster, Recycler, Main Injector, PIP-II), the NuMI and BNB targets, the LBNF near site and the DUNE near detector hall.
